title: fix(sync): confirm each retirement candidate against GitHub instead of vetoing the whole repo
description:
Closes #54.

## The problem

`sync --full` retires mirrored issues GitHub no longer lists, so a transferred issue's source row doesn't linger as a ghost. (Ghosts are harmful: the row freezes at `state='OPEN'` forever and pairs with its own transferred copy at cosine ~1.0, so dedup proposes closing the **live** issue as a duplicate of one that no longer exists.)

To avoid deleting live data, that came with a whole-repo veto: if GitHub reported more issues than the walk saw, retire nothing. **That veto misfires on exactly the repos it matters for.** The walk pages `UPDATED_AT DESC`, so an issue commented on mid-walk jumps to an already-visited page and is absent from the walk while being perfectly alive. `rstudio/shiny` is ~56 pages of issues over minutes of wall time — a single comment in that window trips it. Reconciliation would rarely, perhaps never, run there.

It was also blind to the failure it was written for: a **partially truncated** response leaves the walk's count self-consistent with a smaller repo, so the comparison passes and everything past the truncation point is deleted.

## The fix

Absence from the walk now only makes an issue a *candidate*. `confirm_retirable` then asks GitHub about that one issue, and the row is deleted only on a confident answer:

| Response | Verdict | Action |
|---|---|---|
| 404 | `gone` | retire |
| 200, repository differs from the one queried | `transferred` | retire, logging the destination |
| 200, repository matches | `live` | **keep** — the walk simply missed it |
| read failed | `unknown` | **keep** — a rate limit is not absence |

This is strictly stronger than the count comparison: every deletion is now justified by a direct statement from GitHub about that specific issue, which also closes the truncation hole (truncated pages yield candidates that are still live, and each is individually refused).

## Verified against live GitHub, not assumed

The premise — that a confirmation read distinguishes a *transferred* issue from a *deleted* one — was checked before being built on. Transferred issues leave gaps in the source repo's numbering, so I enumerated `rstudio/thematic` (158 numbers present, max 165 → 7 gaps) and probed each:

- `thematic#145` → 200 → `rstudio/shiny#3902`. Corroborated independently: that issue's timeline carries a `TRANSFERRED_EVENT` naming `rstudio/thematic`.
- `thematic#44` → 200 → `rstudio/bslib#83`.
- `thematic#133`–`#137` → 404.

## Cost

Reads scale with candidates, not repo size, and candidates are normally zero. `thematic` has 7 gaps across ~15 years, so a full sync there spends ~7 extra requests. For scale: the active 4-repo pilot is a ~30-request full sync; the full 41-repo fleet ~767.

## Circuit breakers retained

Two whole-repo refusals remain, both about the walk rather than the issues:

- **Empty response** — the walk saw nothing while the mirror holds rows.
- **Implausible candidate share** — more than `RETIRE_MAX_SHARE` (10%) of mirrored issues missing at once, which also avoids spending a read per candidate to reject hundreds one at a time.

⚠️ **A judgement call worth reviewing:** a strict 10% cap makes retirement impossible on small repos (2 mirrored rows → 10% is 0.2, so any single retirement exceeds it). So there's a `RETIRE_MIN_ALLOWANCE = 5` floor. The effective allowance is `max(5, 10% of mirrored rows)`. The floor wasn't in the original spec discussion — flagging it explicitly rather than burying it.

`totalCount` stays in the query and the log as diagnostic context explaining *why* candidates exist, but is no longer a veto.

## A test-hygiene fix that fell out of this

An autouse fixture now fails any test in this module that reaches the real `gh` transport. It immediately caught **several pre-existing tests silently depending on the network** — passing only because the fake repo `r/a` 404s, which reads as "gone". They were asserting a confirmed deletion while confirming nothing. All now inject a fake confirmer.

## Verification

`make check` (validate-yaml, compile-scripts, py-check, js-check) passes: **451 tests**, up from 437. Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-27-reconcile-confirmation-read-design.md`.

## Follow-up

#57 covers persisting the `old -> new` mapping the redirect reveals, so a transferred issue isn't re-analyzed from scratch in its new home and the review app's Transfers worklist can resolve itself. Deliberately out of scope here — this PR uses the destination only to justify a retirement and make the log legible.

title: feat: implement cross_repo_option — link-duplicate, suggest-transfer, and mirror reconciliation
description:
## What and why

The dedup stage has always asked the model, for duplicate pairs spanning two repositories, for a `cross_repo_option` of `close-and-link` / `keep-both-link` / `transfer`. That value was computed, stored in `dedup_verdicts`, displayed to reviewers — and **never acted on**. Every cross-repo duplicate got identical treatment.

This gives the field meaning. `proposals.build` now maps each value to a **distinct action**, so an action name always describes what approving it does:

| `cross_repo_option` | action | executor plans |
|---|---|---|
| `close-and-link`, or `null` | `close-duplicate` | comment + close `not planned` — **unchanged** |
| `keep-both-link` | `link-duplicate` | comment linking the sibling, **no close** |
| `transfer` | `suggest-transfer` | adds `wrong location`; **a human moves the issue** |

Same-repo pairs are untouched — still GitHub's native duplicate close.

**The system gains no ability to transfer an issue.** `src/triage_verse/gh.py` is byte-identical to `main`, `transferIssue` appears nowhere in `src/`, and neither new action is in `autonomy.ELIGIBLE` or `executor.AUTO_ELIGIBLE`. Tests assert all of that, including that the guard's wire-field backstop refuses `transferIssue` even when smuggled under an allow-listed operation name.

## Root cause of the dead field

The three option names appeared in **no prompt, rubric, or taxonomy** — the only other occurrence of "transfer" in the repo was the rubric line forbidding auto-transfer. The model was picking from an undefined enum, so the stored values were noise. Defining them in the dedup prompt was the prerequisite, not polish.

## The UI is the feature

Because the executor never transfers, approving a `suggest-transfer` only applies a label — and approved proposals leave the queue. Without somewhere to land, every approved suggestion would vanish with nobody having moved anything. So there's a **Transfers** tab: a worklist of suggestions whose label has actually been applied, each with its destination and a *Mark transferred* control.

## A prerequisite bug this exposed

Making `transfer` actionable made an existing latent bug reachable. When an issue is transferred, GitHub gives it a new number in the target repo and it leaves the source. Sync is upsert-only, so the source row froze at `state='OPEN'` **forever**. That ghost then paired with its own transferred copy — byte-identical title and body, cosine ~1.0 against a 0.80 threshold — and dedup would propose **closing the live issue as a duplicate of one that no longer exists**, or transferring it back.

Full syncs now diff the mirrored set against GitHub and delete what vanished (row, comments, and embedding — the row must go, because `embed_repo` has no state filter and would otherwise re-create the vector). Two guards prevent deleting live data: reconciliation refuses when GitHub reports more issues than the walk saw, and refuses outright when a repo returns zero issues while the mirror holds rows.

Reconciliation runs on **full syncs only** — an incremental walk stops at its cursor, so absence there means nothing.

## Review notes

- `decisions/2026-07-27-absent-from-mirror-is-not-reviewable.md` records that this **reverses a documented decision** in the Plan 3 review-queue design ("absence isn't evidence the issue is closed"). The old spec is untouched, per the house rule that specs are immutable.
- `undo` now reverses both new actions. It previously could not — `_reverse_mutations` dispatches on *action*, not mutation *kind* — and worse, reported success while doing nothing and poisoned the record so a corrected undo would skip it.
- Rebased onto main after #40 landed; `record_transferred` takes `decided_by` and the app supplies `current_actor()`, attributing the confirming actor rather than whoever approved.

## Known limitations, deliberately not fixed here

- On a busy repo the `totalCount` guard may **chronically refuse**, since any issue commented on mid-walk trips it. Direction is fail-safe (deletes nothing, logs loudly) but ghost cleanup may rarely fire on the largest repos. A targeted re-check of only the missing candidates is the fix.
- An approved `suggest-transfer` whose execution never happens or errors appears in neither the queue nor the Transfers panel.
- Coverage is limited to issues dedup paired **across repositories**. A plainly misfiled issue that duplicates nothing gets no suggestion — that needs a per-issue classification signal and a separate design.

## Verification

`make check` (validate-yaml, compile-scripts, py-check, js-check) passes: **437 tests**, ruff and pyright clean.

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-27-transfer-suggestion-design.md` · Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-27-cross-repo-option.md`

title: feat: record decided_by + reason on review decisions (#40)
description:
Closes #40

## Summary
Every human review decision now records **who** decided (`decided_by`) and, on reject/edit, **why** (`reason`), so the append-only decision log is audit-ready as the program adds reviewers and autonomy. `decisions.record()` gains a required `decided_by` keyword and an optional `reason` (written only when non-empty; no migration — readers already use `dict.get`). A cached `decisions.current_actor()` resolves the reviewer identity via `gh api user` → `$USER` → `"unknown"` (never raises; passes the egress guard as a REST read). The review app stamps the actor on all three human paths (`on_decide`, `approve_visible`, `app_audit_reject`), captures an optional reason via a modal on every reject, and seeds the edit modal's reason from the agent's proposal rationale. Automated `execute --auto` is intentionally unchanged (`decided_by="autonomy"`), so `autonomy.py`'s `!= "autonomy"` precision filter is unaffected.

Live verification surfaced two Shiny module-namespacing bugs, fixed here: opening a modal from a Queue row (a Shiny module) namespaced the modal input ids, so the top-level save handler never fired. Task 4 regressed the row **Reject** button this way (silent no-op); the row **Edit** button had the same latent bug pre-existing. Both now route through a shared `_module_modal_relay(opener)` factory that builds the modal in the top-level session. Keyboard/drawer paths were already top-level and unchanged.

## Verification
- `make py-check` — ruff format+lint, pyright (0 errors), 356 tests pass.
- Live review app (seeded mirror + proposals, driven in a browser): approve writes `decided_by` with no `reason`; reject (row + drawer) writes `rejected` + `decided_by` + optional `reason`; edit (row) opens with `reason` seeded from the rationale and writes `edited` with edited `params`, original `proposed_params`, and `reason`. Inspected `.data/decisions/*.jsonl` each time.

title: feat(db): retain decision history via append-only classifications and dedup verdicts (#20)
description:
Closes #20

## Summary
Converts the two decision tables (`classifications`, `dedup_verdicts`) from current-state upserts to append-only history so the live mirror is the complete record — no more archiving old DB snapshots to answer "what did triage decide last run." Each table's primary key is widened with `run_id`, so every analyze run writes a new history row. Within a single run the `recheck` stage still refines that run's row (`store()` keeps `ON CONFLICT … UPDATE` on the widened key), giving **one row per run** rather than per store. Two new views (`classifications_latest`, `dedup_verdicts_latest`) return the newest row per key; current-verdict read paths (`db.get_classification`, `db.get_dedup_verdict`, and `tier1`'s "fixed" detection) now read the views, so behavior is unchanged. `proposals.build()` intentionally stays on the base tables filtered by `run_id` — it builds from the run just completed, which is already exactly one row per key. Existing databases are migrated in place by a `PRAGMA user_version`-gated rebuild in `db.connect()` that preserves current rows as the first history entry per key. Spec and plan live under `docs/superpowers/`.

## Verification
`make py-check` (ruff + pyright + 359 pytest) passes. New coverage: append-across-runs, recheck-within-run (one row), latest-view reads, full-history query, migration (preserve + idempotent + fresh-DB), and tier1 latest-signal. To see history: run `analyze` twice over an issue whose content changed, then `SELECT run_id, model, priority, at FROM classifications WHERE repo=? AND number=? ORDER BY at` returns both verdicts while `classifications_latest` returns only the newest.
